item.title: CISA confirms Microsoft SharePoint RCE vulnerability CVE-2026-50522 exploited in ransomware attacks
item.description:
Federal cybersecurity regulators have issued updated threat advisories confirming that active ransomware operators are exploiting a critical remote code execution vulnerability in on-premises collaboration servers. Threat actors leverage unauthenticated network requests to hijack application session parameters and deploy network wide extortion payloads.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-50522 with a CVSS score of 9.8, affects Microsoft SharePoint Server installations. Threat monitoring telemetry confirms that extortion groups issue unauthenticated requests against sign-in endpoints to trigger untrusted deserialization subroutines. By extracting IIS machine keys, attackers generate persistent authentication cookies that survive binary patching, allowing them to impersonate system administrators and deploy ransomware across connected subnets.
Subverting a centralized document collaboration server compromises core identity boundaries across enterprise environments. Because compromised IIS machine keys enable threat actors to sign and decrypt viewstate parameters independently, an adversary retains administrative session access, neutralizing perimeter access controls.
- Apply cumulative security updates provided by Microsoft across all on-premises SharePoint Server farms immediately. - Execute mandatory key rotation procedures for all IIS machine keys across exposed SharePoint farms to invalidate captured session tokens. - Restrict network visibility to SharePoint administrative endpoints by placing instances behind pre-authenticated zero trust reverse proxies. - Inspect web server ingress logs for single-request POST queries targeting deserialization endpoints.
Enterprise collaboration platform protection demands immediate patch installation combined with cryptographic credential rotation to ensure intercepted machine keys cannot maintain persistent backdoor channels. #CodeDefence #Microsoft #SharePoint #RCE #Ransomware #MachineKeys #CISA #KEV

item.title: Metabase releases urgent patches for zero day SQL injection vulnerability CVE-2026-72898 exploited in wild
item.description:
Emergency software updates and reverse-engineered technical analyses have been published for a critical business intelligence platform following confirmed zero day data theft attacks. The flaw permits remote unauthenticated network actors to inject raw SQL directives into application database queries.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-72898, impacts Metabase releases from version 1.58 through 1.63. The issue resides within the reset_password API handler where incoming JSON parameters undergo Clojure map merging. By supplying an extra user-id key carrying raw HoneySQL directive structures, an unauthenticated attacker bypasses input parameterization. The server compiles the unparameterized payload directly into database queries, yielding blind SQL injection to harvest administrative access tokens and exfiltrate connected database contents.
Compromising a enterprise analytics platform exposes underlying database infrastructure to total exfiltration. Because business intelligence tools hold stored credentials for connected data warehouses and production databases, an unauthenticated compromise grants threat actors direct access to corporate intellectual property and customer records.
- Upgrade self-hosted Metabase instances immediately to patched maintenance builds 63.5, 62.9, 61.11, 60.17, 59.21, or 58.24. - Apply temporary workarounds by blocking public access to the reset_password API endpoint if immediate patching is delayed. - Inspect application ingress logs for POST requests targeting reset_password endpoints returning HTTP 400 status codes followed by administrative user queries. - Rotate all database connection credentials and API tokens stored within Metabase application settings.
Business intelligence software security relies on strict query parameterization and prompt zero day patch deployment to ensure corporate reporting tools remain completely insulated from unauthenticated SQL injection. #CodeDefence #Metabase #SQLi #ZeroDay #DataTheft #AppSec #CloudSecurity #VulnerabilityManagement

item.title: China linked Storm-1175 group weaponizes N-able N-central auth bypass CVE-2026-18577 to deploy StormEncryptor
item.description:
Threat intelligence advisories warn that a financially motivated threat cluster has begun weaponizing a recently disclosed remote management console vulnerability in supply chain extortion attacks. The campaign leverages an unauthenticated login bypass to gain full console control and deploy custom ransomware across downstream managed client endpoints.
The operation, attributed to Storm-1175, targets N-able N-central remote monitoring and management servers via CVE-2026-18577. The vulnerability provides unauthenticated actors with full administrative rights over the management platform. Attackers execute automated scripts across connected client endpoints to deploy a new ransomware variant called StormEncryptor, locking client systems and exfiltrating corporate file directories.
Subverting a managed service provider console creates cascading supply chain compromises across hundreds of client networks. Because remote management servers maintain elevated system agent access on client machines, a single compromised management console allows threat actors to execute ransomware commands simultaneously across all managed client environments.
- Force immediate installation of cumulative hotfix build 2026.3.1.7 across all N-able N-central server installations. - Isolate N-central administrative web portals behind zero trust conditional access boundaries to restrict public internet routing. - Audit downstream client endpoints for unrecognized background processes executing StormEncryptor binaries or modified remote management daemons. - Review administrative account rosters and API key registries on management servers for unauthorized credential additions.
Remote management plane resilience demands emergency hotfix deployment combined with strict zero trust interface controls to ensure central MSP platforms cannot be subverted into automated supply chain intrusion vectors. #CodeDefence #Nable #Ncentral #RMM #AuthBypass #StormEncryptor #Ransomware #SupplyChain #AppSec
